A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Neural Conditional Transport Maps, with matching authors, mathematical framework, and retained experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A.1–A.5 are readable and support comparison despite extensive expansion and reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original architecture and conditioning ablations, synthetic-distribution and MNIST transport results, climate-damage generation, and RICE50+ sensitivity analysis, including supplementary results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds evaluated CondOT baselines and quantitative and qualitative class-conditional MNIST generation results.

M1.justification: The hypernetwork, encoder-decoder architecture, discrete embeddings, positional encoding, pretraining losses, and alternating optimization remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 and Appendix A.1 retain the same procedure. The added MNIST application uses already-supported convolutional architectures and conditioning.

E1.justification: V2 adds noise-to-image generation conditioned on all ten MNIST classes, beyond v1's unconditional digit-2-to-digit-3 transport experiment. This substantially extends demonstrated conditional-task coverage into images. Although Section 4.3 mentions continuous attributes, Table 1 explicitly identifies the reported MNIST experiment as having no continuous conditioning input.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds CondOT Default and CondOT Adapted as evaluated comparators on climate damages and RICE50+ GSA; v1 only discussed CondOT without reporting its scores. The existing conditioning alternatives and simplex reference remain. CondOT is explicitly excluded from MNIST evaluation.

E3.justification: New comparisons introduce parameter- and epoch-matched CondOT configurations, retaining CondOT-specific optimization and contrasting discretized versus mixed conditioning. The added MNIST experiment uses class-conditioned generation evaluated with FID and classification accuracy. Existing experimental settings are retained; the newly stated climate split and IAM sample count are disclosures rather than established protocol changes.

E4.justification: V2 extends component ablation into conditional image generation, testing removal of pretraining, shared embeddings, and alternative conditioning mechanisms. Table 1 and new Figure 6 add quantitative evidence and visible artifact comparisons for these choices. The earlier unconditional ablations and appendix implementation analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the 1,000 climate bootstrap replicates, climate uncertainty intervals, appendix distribution plots, and GSA estimator. V2 adds no repeated-training run counts, seeds, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates for its new comparison scores.

E6.justification: Existing Figure 3 and climate/IAM Table 1 scores are retained. New CondOT Default/Adapted entries report climate Wasserstein distances of 0.322/0.255 and IAM correlations of 0.025/0.389, alongside unchanged proposed-method values of 0.170 and 0.942. New conditional MNIST results include FID 2.509 and accuracy 1.000. These are added comparisons and task results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The OT formulations, conditional objective, assumptions, and Appendix A.3 sensitivity-index definition and estimator remain mathematically unchanged. V2 repeats existing GSA definitions and properties in Section 4.2; this does not introduce a new theorem, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The central conditional-NOT, hypernetwork, and GSA contributions remain. V2 newly claims the first comparison of NOT with established solvers for GSA and explicitly includes conditional image generation among its contributions. Its conclusion drops v1's assertion of maintaining theoretical guarantees, with convergence and approximation guarantees instead identified as future work.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of normalization methods' effectiveness for images and explicitly limits extrapolation from MNIST to large-scale image generation. It also identifies missing convergence and approximation analysis. Conversely, Section 5.2.2 removes v1's caveat that neural and simplex cost magnitudes may not be comparable, while retaining Figure 5.

D1.justification: V1 promises future code/data release; v2 states release and supplies a repository link. V2 also discloses the stratified 80/20 climate split, 10,000 IAM evaluations, automatic mixed precision, and CondOT comparison configurations. These materially expand reproducibility information, while Appendix A.1's existing hyperparameters remain unchanged. Repository availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: V2 adds flow-matching and rectified-flow context, additional application references, and more specific discussion of conditional OT flows' optimization and input-distribution restrictions. The central positioning as a flexible conditional extension of NOT remains. Wang's 2025 publication corresponds to the already-cited 2023 work, rather than a distinct new method.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Background becomes four subsections; applications and experimental setup are separated from results; and a computational discussion section is added. Method explanations are substantially expanded, although the appendix prose is largely retained.

P2.justification: V2 adopts TMLR typography, headers, and a wider layout, with enlarged and repositioned existing displays. Table 1 gains CondOT columns, a MNIST results block, and an expanded caption; new Figure 6 presents a multirow digit-generation comparison. V1's appendix Figures 6–8 remain as Figures 7–9.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation: direct CondOT comparisons address v1's lack of an evaluated external conditional-OT baseline, and conditional MNIST ablations test the central conditioning claims beyond scientific data. Added experimental disclosures and the reported code/data release improve reproducibility information. These gains outweigh localized regressions, particularly removal of the GSA cost-magnitude caveat despite unchanged Figure 5 and ambiguity about MNIST attribute conditioning.
